evidence_reviewed: ES query covering the injection window
Health witness log: zero DOWN events for the entire 60s window (3x the first rep duration) -- confirms this is not a 20s-window artifact
Funnel counts essentially identical to the 20s rep: 14 submitted, 12 validated, 11 routed, 11 settled -- normal throughput
No redis-related messages, no ERROR-level entries
reasoning_trace: Second rep of REDIS_OUTAGE, duration tripled (20s->60s) specifically to test whether the first reps null result was a duration artifact. It was not: identical null result at 60s. This replicates and strengthens the finding rather than being a new one -- the systems resilience to redis unavailability (fail-open/retry on the idempotency and payment-status code paths) holds over a meaningfully longer outage window, not just a brief blip. No hypothesis can be formed from this evidence.
blind_conclusion: ABSTAIN -- no detectable evidence anywhere in the window, replicated at 3x duration
confirmation_basis: Not applicable. Second consecutive evidence-free result for REDIS_OUTAGE, now at two different durations (20s and 60s) -- this is a real, replicated finding (system genuinely resilient to redis outages at this scale) not a single-rep fluke. Recommend either instrumenting redis-dependent code paths directly (e.g. log a message when idempotency check falls back due to connection failure) to make this fault type usable, or retiring it as a gold-case source and keeping it only as a documented resilience finding.
